definitions: A type of white blood cell that engulfs and digests cellular debris, foreign substances, microbes, cancer cells, and anything else that does not have the type of proteins specific to healthy body cells on its surface.
Large phagocytic cells found in stationary form in the tissues or as mobile white blood cells, especially at sites of infection.
examples: Macrophages play a crucial role in the immune system.
The macrophages engulfed the invading bacteria.
Tissue macrophages are derived from monocytes.
